transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November after the U.S. midterm elections.
That, according to a person briefed on the matter speaking to NPR from Tel Aviv, NPR's Daniel Estrin has the story.
The person briefed on the U.S. and Israel's war planning spoke to NPR on condition of anonymity to discuss the preparations.
The person said Israel had initially planned to strike Iran in mid-October about two weeks before Israeli elections October 27, but President Trump objected.
The person briefed said the U.S. is now amassing forces in the region to be ready for an attack by early November, after U.S. midterms November 3,
but that these preparations could also be part of a campaign to pressure Iran to reach a diplomatic deal.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is campaigning for reelection on a threat to topple Iran's regime. Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The plans in Saudi Arabia are keeping investors on edge. Brand crude, the global benchmark gained sharply, while stock markets from Tokyo to Hong Kong declined overnight.
In the U.S., another factor is the tumble in A.I. stocks such as Nvidia amid continued concerns about the huge spending being done by companies across the sector.
U.S. bond markets, though, which had taken a hit earlier this year, are rising as investors are opting for an investment that has traditionally been seen as safer.
Rafael Nelm in PR News.
Democrats have a big advantage in the latest Harvard youth poll. Among Gen Zers who say they're definitely voting this fall, 63 percent plan to vote for Democrats,
compared to just a quarter-voting Republican and 1 in 10 who are undecided.
There's also an enthusiasm gap, with more young Democrats than young Republicans saying they're definitely going to vote.
But overall, only one-third of Gen Z plans to vote, which is down from 40 percent ahead of the 2018 and 2022 midterms.
What's more, most young people remain unhappy with the state of the country, with just 9 percent saying they feel the country is headed in the right direction, a record low for the poll.
Alaina Moore, NPR News.
The Nasdaq is down now 655 points, or nearly 2.5 percent. It's NPR News.
The Migration Policy Institute is out with a new report that finds deportations are on pace to reach 660,000 since last October.
It's posting a 26 percent increase in deportations since the Biden administration. However, the organization says the number is below the nearly 1.9 million deportations recorded in 2000 during the Clinton administration.
Mortgage rates have come down since last week. The finance giant Freddie Mac says a 30-year fixed rate mortgage has fallen to 7.32 percent from 7.4, and the 15-year loan averages 6.68 percent.
People in the market for buying a home may be running up against high rates and high prices, but they're also finding more options.
National Association of Realtors' inventory increased to 1.6 million.
There's a new heavyweight pumpkin champion, NPR's Eva Phukach spoke with the man who grew the world's first ever 3,000-pound pumpkin.
Rhode Island gardener Ron Wallace has grown giant pumpkins for more than 30 years. His prize winner weighed in at 3,156 pounds.
So how do you squash the competition? Wallace says the key is genetics.
This hobby is very scientific and soil biology and using different growth hormones for cell division and cell elongation, which will help the pumpkin grow to get to maximum size.
Wallace says he'll harvest the seeds from the pumpkin and donate them to growers' clubs across the country. And then a team will attempt to turn the world's largest pumpkin into the world's largest jack-o'-lantern.
Eva Phukach, NPR News.

Oil prices rise and Asian stock markets decline over Saudi Arabia and Iran tensions
Tech stocks such as Nvidia fall amid concerns over AI sector spending
Harvard youth poll shows Gen Z favoring Democrats, with low voter enthusiasm and pessimism
Migration Policy Institute reports deportations on pace to reach 660,000 since last October
Mortgage rates fall slightly, with 30-year fixed averaging 7.32 percent per Freddie Mac
Rhode Island gardener Ron Wallace grows 3,156-pound record pumpkin
